# App icon: `jl-app-icon`

An app's own icon: its glyph in white on the brand's blue, one family for every SyWare app.

- Class `JlAppIcon`, an atom: `import { JlAppIcon } from '@syware/jlib';`
- On the site: https://bioleyl.github.io/jlib/components/app-icon

Every SyWare app has its own icon, in one family: the app's glyph in white on a rounded tile of the
brand's blue. It tells the apps apart where a word does not fit (a folded side nav, a phone's top bar, a browser tab,
a phone's home screen), and the family says they come from the same place. The SyWare mark stays the company's: the
sign-in panel and the documentation.

Beside the wordmark at the top of the side nav, the icon is decorative; alone, give it a label, the app's name. The
tile looks the same in both themes, as a favicon does. The favicon and the home screen icon are the same tile, drawn
as files: see the Logo page. `setFavicon('workflow')` makes the tile the page's favicon, in the theme's
`--jl-brand`, so an app on its own theme shows it in the browser's tab too.

## Use

```ts
import { JlAppIcon } from '@syware/jlib';
```

```tsx
<JlAppIcon icon="package" size={28} />
```

```html
<jl-app-icon icon="package" size="28"></jl-app-icon>
```

## Properties

Inputs: a JSX prop sets one, code calls `.set(value)` and `.get()`, HTML writes the attribute (lists and objects as JSON).

- `icon` (attribute `icon`): `string`, default `''`. The app's glyph: a registered icon name.
- `size` (attribute `size`): `number`, default `28`. The tile's side, in pixels; the glyph and the corners follow.
- `label` (attribute `label`): `string`, default `''`. The app's name for screen readers, when no wordmark beside it says it.

## Methods

- `setFavicon(icon: string): void`: A function, not a method: makes the app's icon the page's favicon, the tile of a registered icon name in the theme's --jl-brand and --jl-on-brand, so a page's own theme shows in the browser's tab too.

## Styling

- `base` (part, `::part(base)`): The tile.

## Examples

HTML as the site renders it, with its layout classes (`row`, `stack`, `narrow`, `muted`), which are not jlib's: a view writes the same components by class in JSX. A script's `root` is the example's element.

### With the wordmark

At the top of the side nav, beside the wordmark.

```html
<div class="row" style="gap: 24px">
  <span class="row" style="gap: 10px"><jl-app-icon icon="workflow"></jl-app-icon><span style="font-weight: 800; font-size: 18px; letter-spacing: -0.02em">sw<span style="color: var(--jl-brand)">ai</span></span></span>
  <span class="row" style="gap: 10px"><jl-app-icon icon="package"></jl-app-icon><span style="font-weight: 800; font-size: 18px; letter-spacing: -0.02em">sw<span style="color: var(--jl-brand)">stock</span></span></span>
</div>
```

### Sizes

Alone it names the app for screen readers; the sizes of a top bar, a nav and a home screen.

```html
<div class="row" style="align-items: end">
  <jl-app-icon icon="package" size="20" label="swstock"></jl-app-icon>
  <jl-app-icon icon="package" size="28" label="swstock"></jl-app-icon>
  <jl-app-icon icon="package" size="44" label="swstock"></jl-app-icon>
  <jl-app-icon icon="package" size="64" label="swstock"></jl-app-icon>
</div>
```
